To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the photochemical reaction of the porous coordination polymer (PCPs) is affected by the reaction of the porous crystalline material.

a two-dimensional porous framework with interdigitated channels undergoes photochemical [2+4] cycloadditions in a single-crystalline manner, resulting in the formation of a three-dimensional framework with a one-dimensional channel.

the photochemical [2+ 2] cyclo-addition reactions in a crystalline framework proceed with single-crystal-to- single-crystal transformation and one-dimensional channels of a crystalline framework show structural changes that impact CO(2) uptake.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of porous coordination polymers with a high degree of structural and functional complexity.
the development of porous coordination polymers (PCPs), a new class of crystalline materials, which are built up by coordination bonds between metal ions or clusters and multidentate ligands.
the design and synthesis of new materials for gas sorption and separation applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CO(2), N(2), and Ar gas sorption behavior of the [2+2]-cycloaddition product was different from the starting porous coordination polymer.

the photochemical [2+ 2] cyclo-addition reaction of the porous coordination polymer (PCP) 2,5-bis(2-pyridyl)terephthalate (BPT) in the presence of a small amount of CO2 leads to a significant change in the sorption behavior for CO2 and N2.
the CO2 sorption capacity of the cycloadduct is significantly lower than that of the starting material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
photochemical reactions in the porous crystalline framework can be used for the modification of the framework structure and the resulting properties.
the photochemical cycloadditions on the pore surface impact the sorption behavior, and this impact is dependent on the dimensionality of the channels.

photochemical [2+4] cycloadditions of a porphyrin ligand with a 2-ethylpyridine ligand in a two-dimensional porous framework of a porous coordination network (PCN-14) proceed via a single-crystal to single-crystal (SCSC) manner, and the resulting framework shows an enhanced CO2 uptake of 2.4 mmol g(-1) (1 bar at 273 K), which is 1.6-fold higher
The main takeaway from our work is that
a photochemical reaction can be used to modify the structure and properties of porous materials.
the photochemistry of a crystalline porous coordination polymer can be used to tune the sorption of CO(2) in the pores.
the photochemical reaction of the framework is not limited to the interior of the pores, but also occurs on the pore surfaces of the framework.
